Thanks Lauren — I ran the SIG export this morning from the compliance repo. Notes:
- Total uncompressed PDF bundle ~1.5GB. I split into two printable PDF parts: part01 = 780MB, part02 = 720MB. Both are linearized for faster web open and flattened (no form data).
- Generated SHA256 checksums and a manifest: SIG-export-checksum.txt (format below).
- Stamped each PDF footer with "Redwood Inference - Confidential - Exported 2027-05-02" for audit traceability.

Manifest (first lines):
part01.pdf, SIG-export-part01.pdf, SHA256: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...
part02.pdf, SIG-export-part02.pdf, SHA256: f5c6a2b9d3e4b1f0b7c...

Attachments included: SIG-export-part01.pdf (780MB), SIG-export-part02.pdf (720MB), SIG-export-checksum.txt, split-upload-instructions.pdf

I will upload the two PDFs to our secure Drive folder and share the links; Karthik, can you draft a one-page upload checklist that includes: preferred filename format, recommended UA string for retries, and the OneTrust/Whistic multipart upload steps? Also: note that OneTrust sometimes rejects uploads with the same filename; include a timestamp suffix policy.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Compliance Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

[attachments: SIG-export-part01.pdf (780MB); SIG-export-part02.pdf (720MB); SIG-export-checksum.txt; split-upload-instructions.pdf]
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SIG bundle upload to OneTrust/Whistic for RFP

Great — thanks Marissa. Uploaded the two parts to Drive and tested an upload to OneTrust sandbox. Findings and proposed short script:

- OneTrust: multipart upload accepted for parts <1GB but fails if the client tries to re-upload an identical filename. Use timestamped filenames (YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS) as Marissa suggested.
- Whistic: accepts individual PDFs but rate-limits at 3 concurrent uploads from same IP; slower but reliable.
- If a transfer fails mid-stream, the sandbox supports byte-range resume for HTTP PUT with Content-Range, but only when using the OneTrust API token (not their web UI). We'll include a curl example using a token and a fallback resumable loop.

Upload checklist (one-liner entries in draft):
1) Filename: ACME_SIG_<YYYYMMDD>_part01.pdf
2) Use API token and PUT with Content-Range when available
3) If web UI only: try sequential single-part uploads, wait 30s between retries, include timestamp suffix
4) Verify SHA256 after each upload using our manifest endpoint

Included a tiny bash snippet (in split-upload-instructions.pdf) that: calculates checksum, attempts PUT with range resume, and retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff.

I will push the final instructions to the Drive folder and share links with Acme.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Platform Integrations Engineer | Redwood Inference
